parameters.name: hook_id
parameters.description: Optional Marketing Studio Setup hook id (the 'what' — attention-grabbing mechanic, e.g. 'Object flies into frame'). Use a previously selected hook id from a catalog confirmed compatible with this model. Hooks/settings are supported only for these presets: UGC, Tutorial, Unboxing, Product Review, UGC Virtual Try On. If the user asks for a hook without an id, obtain their choice from an available compatible hook catalog before generating; never invent an id. INDEPENDENT of `setting_id` — you can pass `hook_id` alone, `setting_id` alone, both, or neither. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `ad_reference_id` — hook/setting compose a video from explicit building blocks, while ad_reference recreates an existing video's scenario. Pick one approach, never both.

parameters.name: setting_id
parameters.description: Optional Marketing Studio Setup setting id (the 'where' — location/vibe, e.g. 'Sunlit kitchen, morning light'). Use a previously selected setting id from a catalog confirmed compatible with this model. Hooks/settings are supported only for these presets: UGC, Tutorial, Unboxing, Product Review, UGC Virtual Try On. INDEPENDENT of `hook_id` — you can pass `setting_id` alone, `hook_id` alone, both, or neither. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `ad_reference_id` — see `hook_id` for explanation.

parameters.name: ad_reference_id
parameters.description: Optional ad reference id. When set, the new marketing video follows the analyzed scenario of an existing reference video (scene composition, pacing, hook, narration) instead of inventing a structure from the prompt alone. Use this when the user wants to 'recreate this ad', 'make a video like this', or 'copy the style of this clip'. Supply an existing ad reference id confirmed compatible with this model; do not substitute a media id or preset id from another workflow. AVATAR/PRODUCT ARE NOT AUTO-PULLED: if the ad reference was created with a linked avatar and/or product, those links are stored on the ad_reference for organizational/reference purposes only — they are NOT applied at generation time. The backend executor only reads avatar/product from explicit `avatars` / `product_ids` on this call. Rule: if the user wants the new video to feature the same avatar/product that was linked to the ad_reference (or a different one they specify), you MUST pass them explicitly here as `avatars: [{id, type: 'custom'|'preset'}]` and `product_ids: ['<uuid>']`. Example: ad_reference X was created with Sofia (preset) + On Cloud shoes linked, and the user says 'generate the marketing video' — you still pass `avatars: [{id: <sofia-id>, type: 'preset'}]` and `product_ids: ['<on-cloud-id>']` along with `ad_reference_id`. If the user asks for a different avatar/product than what was linked, just pass the new ones — the ad_reference still drives the scenario. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `hook_id` and `setting_id` — ad_reference replaces the explicit hook/setting composition with a reference-driven scenario. Pick one approach, never both.

parameters.description: Which face to lipsync. true/false turns automatic detection on or off (default off). Or one object: {auto_detect}, {frame_number, coordinates: [x, y]} with a point on the face in that frame, {bounding_boxes: [[x1, y1, x2, y2] | null, ...]} with one box per frame, or {bounding_boxes_url: "https://..."} pointing to JSON with bounding_boxes. video.name: Ad Multiplier Recreate
video.description: Recreate a 4-30 second source ad as a new ad for another audience, language, product, cast or setting, keeping its structure, beats and pacing, or regenerate only its hook, its CTA or both and stitch them back into the source. Everything is decided from the video, the images and the prompt: the backend analyzes the source, classifies the images and writes the generation prompt.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Output resolution: 480p, 720p, or 1080p.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: recreate renders the whole ad again and costs the source length rounded up. sections renders a new hook (4-15 s), CTA (4-5 s) or both, each in its own render, and stitches them in place of the source ones; the rest of the source is kept as is. The run reserves the longest lengths and is charged for the lengths it renders. With both, if one part fails the other is still delivered with the source kept in place of the failed one, and only the delivered part is charged. If the source has no clear hook or CTA, the new one is added before (hook) or after (CTA) the whole source instead.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: With mode sections, which part to regenerate: hook (the opening), cta (the closing call to action) or both. Omit it for recreate.
